description: The other half of a phaser: a chain of up to fifty allpass stages modelled on a light-dependent resistor, swept by a control voltage and mixed against the dry signal

params.text: Reshapes the control voltage before it drives the light-dependent resistor model, raising it to a power between a half and two so the sweep leans to one end; at the centre it passes through unshaped
Mixes the allpass chain against the dry signal, from all dry at the left to all phased at the right
Sets how many allpass stages the signal goes through, 1 to 50; the setting is continuous and the last stage is faded in as the knob passes it

inputs.text: Sweeps the phaser. Five volts is the top of the range and minus five volts the bottom, and a bipolar LFO here is what makes the usual phaser sound.

outputs.text: The mix of the phased and dry signals, at the level it came in

notes: the modulation knob comes up fully anticlockwise, which is all dry, so a new module passes the audio through unchanged until it is turned up.
the control voltage input is what sweeps this module; with nothing patched there the allpass chain stands at one frequency and the sound does not move.
the module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.
